prompt: The illustration shows a cutaway view of a small Hong Kong capsule store at night, with a single robot behind the counter and three simultaneous activities: a customer walking out through a sensor gate with a phone notification showing an automatic bill, another customer frowning at a shelf item that failed to scan while the robot looks on helplessly, and a third customer trying to ask a question the robot cannot answer. Above the ceiling, a dense web of cameras and LIDAR sensors feeds data to a remote human operator visible on a small monitor, who has just pressed an override button; through a back door, a human employee in a uniform rushes in to fix the error. A large promotional screen inside the store plays a polished demo video of the same robot smoothly restocking and greeting customers, but the real scene around it is messy and confused, with a floor-cleaning robot bumping into the stranded customer. The contrast makes visible the entry's core ideas: a spectrum of automation from walk-out billing to robot restocking, the illusion of full autonomy versus hidden human oversight, the goal of cutting labour costs and staying open longer, and the risk that a machine can only follow rules while a person can improvise—and that observing a real store with real confused customers is nothing like a demonstration video.
